carousels.name: Urges get louder before they get quieter

slides.title: The urges are getting worse? [[That can be a good sign.]]
slides.sub: Why habits often fight back hardest right before they fade.

slides.title: The [[last push]]
slides.body: Psychologists call it an extinction burst: when a habit stops getting rewarded, it often gets louder for a while before it fades.

slides.title: Your brain is [[testing]] you
slides.body: "Are you sure? Really sure? What about now?" The louder phase is the habit checking if you'll give in.

slides.title: Giving in [[resets]] the test
slides.body: If the burst gets rewarded, the brain learns: push harder next time. Riding it out teaches the opposite.

slides.title: Get through the [[burst]]
items: Expect it — it's part of the process, not failure.
Double your guardrails this week.
Move your body when it spikes.
Tell someone it's a hard week.
slides.note: Is this week harder than last? Comment YES or NO 👇

slides.title:
Outlast the burst.
[[Win the war.]]
slides.lead: A panic button for the spikes, guided audio sessions and streaks that show how far you've come.

carousels.name: What p*rn actually costs you in hours

slides.title: 30 minutes a day is [[182 hours a year.]]
slides.sub: That's more than 7 full days. Here's what else that time could be.

slides.title: Count it [[honestly]]
slides.body: Not just the minutes watching. The searching, the scrolling, the time lost after feeling flat. For many people, it's a lot more than 30 minutes.

slides.title: Time is the [[hidden]] cost
slides.body: Nobody budgets for it. It just disappears, a little every night. Hours you'll never get back.

slides.title: 182 hours [[could be]]
items: A new language to conversation level.
A fitness transformation — 3 workouts a week, all year.
A side project or a skill that pays.
Dozens of books, or nights out with friends.

slides.title: Get the hours [[back.]]
slides.body: Pick one thing from that list and give it the time the habit used to take. Same hours. Completely different life.
slides.note: What would you do with 182 extra hours? Comment it 👇

slides.title:
Take your
[[time back.]]
slides.lead: Block p*rn completely, track every day and follow a recovery program that fills the time with purpose.

slides.title: Gym at 6 AM. Clean diet. [[Still can't quit this.]]
slides.sub: Why discipline in one area doesn't automatically transfer.

slides.title: It's not a [[character]] problem
slides.body: If you can train, work hard and keep promises elsewhere, you're not lazy or weak. This habit just works differently.

slides.title: Different [[trigger]], different fight
slides.body: The gym is planned. This habit ambushes you — tired, alone, late at night. Discipline works best with a plan. Most guys don't have one for this.

slides.title: Use what [[already works]]
slides.body: You already know how to build a habit: schedule, track, show up. Apply the same system here.

slides.title: Train it like the [[gym]]
items: Have a program, not just motivation.
Track it daily like your workouts.
Plan the hard sessions: late nights, weekends.
Get a spotter: an accountability partner.
slides.note: Disciplined guys: what's the hardest part for you? 👇

slides.title:
You already have the discipline.
[[Now get the system.]]
slides.lead: A step-by-step recovery program, daily habit tracking and 1-on-1 accountability.

carousels.name: You stopped watching but you're still replaying

slides.title: You stopped watching. But your mind [[keeps hitting replay.]]
slides.sub: What to do with the memories and fantasies that pop up.

slides.title: It's [[normal]]
slides.body: Years of images don't vanish in a week. Many people describe flashbacks or fantasies popping up early on. It doesn't mean you're failing.

slides.title: Don't [[fight]] the thought
slides.body: Trying hard not to think about something often makes it louder. Notice it, name it — "just a memory" — and shift your attention.

slides.title: Don't [[feed]] it either
slides.body: Lingering on the fantasy is like rewatching in your head. The goal: notice, don't entertain.

slides.title: When it [[pops up]]
items: Label it: "That's an old memory."
Change your focus: stand up, move, talk.
Engage your hands: cook, write, train.
Expect it to fade as the weeks go on.
slides.note: Does this happen to you too? Comment "same" 👇

slides.title:
Clear the screen
[[in your head too.]]
slides.lead: Guided audio sessions, journaling for patterns and an AI coach when your mind won't quiet down.

slides.title: Seeing a therapist about this [[isn't weakness.]]
slides.sub: It's one of the smartest moves you can make.

slides.title: It's not [[just]] about p*rn
slides.body: For many people, the habit sits on top of something: stress, loneliness, anxiety, old pain. A therapist helps you work on what's underneath.

slides.title: Athletes have [[coaches]]
slides.body: Nobody calls a pro athlete weak for having a coach. A therapist is a coach for your mind.

slides.title: They've heard it [[before]]
slides.body: You won't shock them. Compulsive sexual behavior is something many clinicians work with. No judgment — that's the job.

slides.title: Getting [[started]]
items: Look for therapists who work with compulsive behaviors.
Ask about online sessions if in-person feels like too much.
Be honest in the first session — it saves time.
Use self-help tools alongside, not instead.
slides.note: Would you ever consider therapy for this? Be honest 👇

slides.title:
Support between
[[sessions.]]
slides.lead: An AI coach for anytime guidance, daily journaling and a community — alongside professional care, not instead of it.
